title: Jack and the beanstalk.
lines: Once upon a time there was a boy called Jack.
He lived with his mummy in a little house.
They were very poor.
All they had left was a cow, and that cow didn't give milk anymore.
Jack, said Mummy, go to the market and sell our cow.
Then we can buy food.
Jack set off with the cow.
On the way he met a strange old man.
What a lovely cow, said the man.
I'll swap her for five magic beans.
Magic beans!
Jack thought that was amazing, and he swapped the cow.
But when he got home, Mummy was cross.
Five beans for our cow?
And she threw the beans out of the window.
That night something magical happened.
The beans began to grow.
They grew and grew, higher than the house, higher than the trees, all the way up into the clouds.
The next morning Jack looked out of the window.
Wow!
A beanstalk up to the sky!
Jack began to climb.
He climbed and climbed, higher and higher, through the clouds.
And above the clouds he saw a big castle.
He knocked on the door.
A big woman opened it.
She was a giant's wife.
Quick, hide, she said.
My husband the giant is coming!
Boom, boom, boom.
The ground shook.
Here came the giant.
He was as big as a tree.
He sniffed.
Fee, fi, fo, fum, I smell a human child!
But his wife said: No, you can smell the soup.
Eat up.
The giant ate his soup and then he took a hen out of a cage.
Lay!
said the giant.
And the hen laid an egg.
A golden egg!
Then the giant took a golden harp.
Play!
And the harp played a lovely song all by itself.
The giant got tired and fell asleep.
Snore, snore!
Jack crept out of his hiding place.
He tucked the hen under his arm.
But when he picked up the harp, the harp shouted: Master!
Master!
Help!
The giant woke up.
Grrrr!
Jack ran as fast as he could to the beanstalk, and climbed down.
Mummy, quick, the axe!
Mummy gave Jack the axe, and chop, chop, chop, the beanstalk fell down.
The giant had to stay up there, in his cloud castle.
He could never come down again.
From that day on the hen laid a golden egg every day.
Jack and his mummy were never poor again.
They even bought their cow back.
And in the evening the golden harp played lovely songs for them.
